analysis: The clinical presentation of this patient, including obesity, bilateral papilledema, pulsatile headache, horizontal diplopia, and transient visual obscurations, is highly suggestive of increased intracranial pressure, most likely due to idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). The key diagnostic test to confirm IIH is a lumbar puncture, which measures the opening pressure of the cerebrospinal fluid. An elevated opening pressure would confirm the diagnosis of IIH. Other tests, such as MRI, can help rule out other causes of increased intracranial pressure, but they do not confirm IIH. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, a lumbar puncture is the definitive test to confirm the diagnosis in this scenario.
